fields.name: Śiśir Kumār Ghoṣ (Sisir Kumar Ghosh)
fields.place: Born at Māgurā (Jessore); Calcutta (Amṛta Bazar Patrikā)
fields.works: Amiya Nimāi-carita; Kālācāṅd-gītā; Lord Gaurāṅga (English); founder of the Amṛta Bazar Patrikā (first «Ānanda-bazar Viṣṇupriyā»)
fields.notes: Kāyastha, son of Harinārāyaṇa Ghoṣ and Amṛtamayī, of a zamindār family of Māgurā (Jessore); founded the Amṛta Bazar Patrikā. Turned from jñāna to Gaura-bhakti through his brother Hemanta Bābu (the Prārthanā and the Prema-bhakti-candrikā); walked barefoot chanting Gaurāṅga's name; fainted before his painting of Nitāi-Gaura and Sītānātha. His Amiya Nimāi-carita and Lord Gaurāṅga made many devotees.

fields.place: Guhavaṭī (Murshidabad), by the Gaṅgā: his temple of Gopāla, ākhaḍā and samādhi
fields.notes: Came down the Gaṅgā on a raft to Guhavaṭī with a Deity of Gopāla he had recovered from the river, in the days of Dewan Rājīvalocana Rāya of Kāśimbāzār; the people built him a temple and an ākhaḍā. Took from the Dewan only what his guests needed; once offered only Tulasī leaves and food arrived. After his death he was met in Vṛndāvana and sent a gong to his temple, still worshipped.

A very old bābājī living near Sanātana Gosvāmī's samādhi, who offered bhoga to Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī daily from his mādhukarī; could not sleep on money hidden under his bed («bugs»). At his death he told Sanātana dāsa Bābājī to offer a seat to Lord Caitanya, who had come. (The disciples field said «Sanātana Dāsa Bābājī»; the text does not call him his disciple.)
